title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 11 (Omitted — Historical Commencement of Business)

content.overview: Section 11 of the Companies Act, 2013 (as originally enacted) dealt with commencement of business and was later omitted. The functional regime for commencement of business is now primarily in Section 10A. Exam answers must use current law and not treat the omitted s. 11 as operative. Current commencement-of-business rule is section 10A, not omitted section 11.
content.glance: Note that s. 11 has been omitted; point to s. 10A as the current commencement-of-business provision; warn against relying on repealed text.

sections.heading: Original Role of Section 11
sections.body: As originally enacted, s. 11 regulated commencement of business after incorporation.

sections.heading: Omission
sections.body: Section 11 was omitted by amendment; it is no longer operative.

sections.heading: Current Law — Section 10A
sections.body: Commencement of business is now governed by s. 10A (declaration and office verification).

examples.title: Reliance on omitted section
examples.body: An answer cites s. 11 as the current commencement rule. That is incorrect; s. 11 is omitted and s. 10A applies.

hypotheticals.question: Is Section 11 still good law for commencement of business?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 11 has been omitted. Apply Section 10A.

misconceptions.trap: Section 11 still governs commencement of business.
misconceptions.correction: Section 11 is omitted; the current provision is Section 10A.
